sections.markdown:
## C — Driving situations: reduced visibility, headlights, night, fog, bad weather, snow and ice, and skids

FACT_ID: sec07-F01 | anchor: A27
Visibility means how clearly you can see vehicles, pedestrians, signs, signals and pavement markings, and darkness, fog, heavy rain and snow are its most common reducers. [A27]
Source: [A27 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec07-F02 | anchor: A27
When visibility is reduced, guide yourself by the road's edge lines or its right side. [A27]
Source: [A27 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec07-F03 | anchor: A27
Yellow markings belong on your left, never your right, because yellow divides opposing traffic and marks the road's left edge. [A27]
Why it matters: yellow on your right in poor visibility means you may be on the wrong side.
Source: [A27 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec07-F04 | anchor: A27
White markings show the road's right edge and also divide lanes moving in the same direction. [A27]
Source: [A27 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec07-F05 | anchor: A27
Headlights both help you see in low visibility and help oncoming drivers see you. [A27]
Source: [A27 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec07-F06 | anchor: A27
You must switch on your headlights whenever the light is too poor to see clearly at least 1,000 feet ahead of your vehicle. [A27]
Source: [A27 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec07-F07 | anchor: A27
Night, fog and stormy weather are named as key times to use headlights. [A27]
Source: [A27 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec07-F08 | anchor: A27
Maryland law requires headlights on whenever you run your windshield wipers in inclement weather, meaning bad weather that may make driving unsafe. [A27]
Source: [A27 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec07-F09 | anchor: A27
Use low beams in normal driving such as on a lit street at night, and in fog, rain or snow. [A27]
Source: [A27 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec07-F10 | anchor: A27
Low beams are also advised when entering a tunnel or a construction area; the law does not always demand it, but it helps other drivers and workers see you. [A27]
Source: [A27 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec07-F11 | anchor: A27
High beams are for roads with no streetlights, so you can see other vehicles and people. [A27]
Source: [A27 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec07-F12 | anchor: A27
You must dim to low beams at least 500 feet before you meet an oncoming vehicle. [A27]
Source: [A27 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec07-F13 | anchor: A27
You must also dim to low beams when the vehicle you are following is 300 feet or less ahead. [A27]
Source: [A27 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec07-F14 | anchor: A27
Night driving is riskier because distance and speed of other vehicles are harder to judge and you can see only as far as your headlights reach. [A27]
Source: [A27 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec07-F15 | anchor: A28
At night, do not look straight into oncoming headlights; look at the road ahead or slightly right, toward the right edge of your lane or the road. [A28]
Source: [A28 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec07-F16 | anchor: A28
At night, leave more space behind the vehicle ahead so a sudden stop does not cause a crash. [A28]
Source: [A28 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec07-F17 | anchor: A28
In fog, drive slower than normal, and slow even more when you see headlights or taillights ahead, ready to stop quickly. [A28]
Source: [A28 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec07-F18 | anchor: A28
If fog is too thick to drive safely, pull fully off the road to a safe spot and switch on your emergency flashers. [A28]
Source: [A28 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec07-F19 | anchor: A28
In fog use only low beam headlights, plus fog lights if your vehicle has them. [A28]
Source: [A28 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec07-F20 | anchor: A28
Traction is the grip between tires and road that lets a vehicle start, stop and turn, and wet roads cut traction and raise crash risk. [A28]
Source: [A28 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec07-F21 | anchor: A28
The gap you need behind the car ahead is much larger on wet roads than dry ones, and larger still on snow or ice. [A28]
Source: [A28 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec07-F22 | anchor: A28
In bad weather slow down to gain reaction time, and keep tire tread at the level the tire maker and your vehicle guidelines recommend. [A28]
Source: [A28 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec07-F23 | anchor: A28
Slamming the brakes can start a skid; without an anti-lock braking system, pump the brakes to avoid skidding. [A28]
Source: [A28 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec07-F24 | anchor: A28
In bad weather avoid jerking the wheel or changing speed suddenly. [A28]
Source: [A28 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec07-F25 | anchor: A28
Ramps and bridges ice over before roads do, and plowed roads can refreeze at night or hold icy patches from daytime melt. [A28]
Source: [A28 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec07-F26 | anchor: A29
For bad weather, check that your windshield wipers work well and drive with your headlights on. [A29]
Source: [A29 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec07-F27 | anchor: A29
No speed is completely safe on snow and ice, and each road can differ with sun, shade and how much salt it has. [A29]
Source: [A29 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec07-F28 | anchor: A29
Black ice is a thin, nearly invisible layer of ice on asphalt formed when ice or snow melts and freezes again. [A29]
Source: [A29 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec07-F29 | anchor: A29
Four-wheel drive may give more control, but those vehicles can still slide on ice and snow. [A29]
Source: [A29 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec07-F30 | anchor: A29
Before driving in snow or ice, clear all ice and snow off the vehicle so its windows and lights are clear. [A29]
Source: [A29 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec07-F31 | anchor: A29
On snow or ice, start off very slowly, test your brakes gently, and begin slowing well before an intersection or turn. [A29]
Source: [A29 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec07-F32 | anchor: A29
In winter keep both the gas tank and the windshield washer fluid full. [A29]
Source: [A29 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec07-F33 | anchor: A29
When a snow emergency is declared, use chains, snow tires or radial tires on designated snow emergency routes. [A29]
Source: [A29 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec07-F34 | anchor: A29
A car emergency kit should hold flares, a flashlight with batteries, a first aid kit, a blanket, kitty litter or sand for traction, a small shovel and an ice scraper. [A29]
Source: [A29 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec07-F35 | anchor: A29
Sand, gravel, rough pavement, oil, water and higher speed all reduce traction, which makes a skid or slide more likely. [A29]
Source: [A29 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec07-F36 | anchor: A29
In a skid, first ease off whichever pedal you are pressing, gas or brake, to regain control. [A29]
Source: [A29 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec07-F37 | anchor: A29
Steer in the direction of the skid and look where you want the vehicle to go. [A29]
Why it matters: steering against the skid is the classic wrong answer.
Source: [A29 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec07-F38 | anchor: A29
Brake only after your tires grip the road again, and gentle acceleration may help if the rear wheels lose traction. [A29]
Source: [A29 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0029]

Glossary: visibility — how clearly you can see the road scene [A27]. Inclement weather — bad weather that may make driving unsafe [A27]. Traction — the grip of tires on the road [A28]. Black ice — a thin, hard-to-see ice layer on asphalt [A29].
Memory aid: in a skid, lift, look and steer the way the car is sliding, then brake only once you have grip [A29].
Misconception: high beams do not help in fog; the manual says to use low beams only, plus fog lights if fitted [A28].
